title: Train Wreck (Message Chains)
pattern: A client navigates through a long sequence of nested object references, requesting one object to get another, then another, and so on.
why_bad: It introduces severe coupling between the client and the exact navigation path of the domain model. Any change to the structure of intermediate relationships (e.g., splitting `totals` out of `invoice`) breaks the calling client.
detection: A chain of 3 or more method calls where each method returns an object on which the next method is called (e.g., `a.get_b().get_c().get_d()`).
counterexample: Method chaining on Builder patterns or fluent APIs (like iterators or query builders) where the returned type is a conceptual continuation of the same object.
fix: Hide the delegation by adding a direct method to the root object (e.g., `customer.get_discount_for_order(order_id)`), encapsulating the internal hierarchy.
source: Martin Fowler, *Refactoring* (1999), Chapter 3 ("Message Chains"); Andrew Hunt & David Thomas, *The Pragmatic Programmer* (2019), Topic 36 ("Train Wrecks").
